title: Finite reduced discrete schemes as residue-field coproducts
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], T a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] with finite discrete underlying space, and g:T→Spec k. Suppose at every t the canonical k→κ(t) [def-weil-residue-field] is finite and separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there are n, fields K_a indexed by Fin n, and finite separable embeddings ι_a:k→K_a, together with an isomorphism from the coproduct of Spec K_a [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to T, whose composite with g on the a-th summand is Spec ι_a. The case n=0 is included.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: The canonical map Spec κ(t)→T is a closed immersion because t is closed. Factor it through the singleton open subscheme. This factor is a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme and is therefore an isomorphism. Thus every canonical residue-field map is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: The images are disjoint singletons covering T. The coproduct map is a surjective open immersion and hence an isomorphism. Reindex the finite set of points by Fin n. The canonical residue-field maps commute with g, yielding the asserted scalar equations.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_reduced_discrete_residue_fields
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced T]
    [Finite T] [DiscreteTopology T] (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (hsep : ∀ t : T, (g.residueFieldAlgebraMap t).Finite ∧
      @Algebra.IsSeparable k (T.residueField t) _ _
        (g.residueFieldAlgebraMap t).toAlgebra) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (K : Fin n → Type u) (_ : ∀ a, Field (K a)) (ι : ∀ a, k →+* K a),
      (∀ a, (ι a).Finite ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable k (K a) _ _ (ι a).toAlgebra) ∧
      ∃ e : (∐ fun a : Fin n ↦ Spec (.of (K a))) ≅ T,
        ∀ a : Fin n,
          Sigma.ι (fun b : Fin n ↦ Spec (.of (K b))) a ≫ e.hom ≫ g =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (ι a))
